## Read iris.csv file
```{R}
iris1 <- read.csv("data/iris.csv")
iris1
head(iris1)
```

## Check the limited values which variable 'species' can have
```{R}
levels(iris1$Species)
```

## Update a value to a new value
```{R}
# Try to update the values to a new value which does not exist in the levels. Read the error which you see after running this code
iris1$Species[iris1$Species == 'virginica'] <- 'new.species'

# If you want to add a new value, say 'new.species' in this case, or update the previous values to a new value, you must add new.species to the levels first.
levels(iris1$Species) <- c(levels(iris1$Species), "new.species")

# Check the level, ensure new level is added
levels(iris1$Species)

iris1$Species[iris1$Species == 'virginica'] <- 'new.species'

iris1
```

## Alternative to handle factor
```{R}
#Force R to treat all columns which have string values as string and do not consider any column type as Factor by using parameter stringsAsFactors = FALSE.
iris4 <- read.csv("data/iris.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

# print out string
str(iris4)

iris4$Species[iris4$Species == 'virginica'] <- 'new.species'

# unique value in Species column
unique(iris4$Species)
```
